title: Cut elimination with digging in a linear modal fixed-point calculus
formal: Editorial single-modality variant of the proposed digging extension: in the infinitary linear modal fixed-point calculus defined below, does every valid proof with cuts have a valid cut-free proof of the same end sequent?
definitions:
Formulas are finite expressions generated from atomic pairs p and their duals, fixed-point variables X, the units 1, bottom, 0, top, the binary connectives tensor, par, plus, with, the unary modalities box and diamond, and binders mu X.A and nu X.A. Only closed formulas occur in sequents; bound variables occur positively because there is no negation constructor on variables. Duality exchanges atomic pairs, 1/bottom, 0/top, tensor/par, plus/with, box/diamond and mu/nu, and leaves the bound variable placeholder X unchanged before binding. Substitution for X avoids variable capture. Sequents are finite multisets of formulas, written |-Gamma.

The exact rules, written premises above the implication arrow to the conclusion, are: identity has no premises and concludes |-A,A-dual; cut takes |-A,Gamma and |-A-dual,Delta to |-Gamma,Delta; par takes |-A,B,Gamma to |-A par B,Gamma; tensor takes |-A,Gamma and |-B,Delta to |-A tensor B,Gamma,Delta; each plus rule takes |-Ai,Gamma to |-A1 plus A2,Gamma; with takes |-A,Gamma and |-B,Gamma to |-A with B,Gamma. The 1 rule concludes |-1 with no premises; bottom takes |-Gamma to |-bottom,Gamma; top concludes |-top,Gamma with no premises; there is no rule introducing 0. Each fixed-point rule takes |-A[X:=eta X.A],Gamma to |-eta X.A,Gamma, where eta is mu or nu.

The modal rules are exactly: from |-A,Gamma infer |-box A,diamond Gamma (diamond prefixes each formula in Gamma); from |-Gamma infer |-diamond A,Gamma; from |-diamond A,diamond A,Gamma infer |-diamond A,Gamma; and the added digging rule from |-diamond diamond A,Gamma infer |-diamond A,Gamma. There is no dereliction, no other modality, and no unrestricted weakening or contraction. These choices select a concrete modal instance rather than all super-exponential signatures.

A pre-proof is a possibly infinite, finitely branching tree of these rule instances, with the end sequent at its root. Along a branch moving from conclusion to premise, the ancestor relation links context occurrences to their copies, connective occurrences to the components exposed in that premise, a fixed point to its unfolded body, and modal-rule occurrences to the corresponding unprefixed premise occurrences. Contraction links its principal diamond occurrence to either premise copy; digging links its principal diamond A to diamond diamond A. Weakening has no ancestor for the weakened occurrence. Cut has ancestors only for the context occurrences, not for the removed cut formulas.

A thread follows one occurrence by these links along a tail of a branch. It is valid if it is principal at infinitely many steps and, among the formulas recurring infinitely often along it, there is a least formula under the reflexive syntactic subformula ordering, up to renaming bound variables, whose outermost binder is nu. Least means it is a subformula of every recurring formula. A pre-proof is valid if every infinite branch has such a thread. Finite leaves must be zero-premise rule instances. Proofs need not be regular or computable. The conclusion is existence of a valid cut-free proof; no preservation of regularity or prescribed reduction strategy is required.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked cut-admissibility proof for exactly this infinitary calculus and validity condition, or exhibit a sequent with a valid proof using cuts but no valid cut-free proof. This settles the selected single-modality instance, not the entire parameterized uniform theorem proposed by the source.
context:
Bauer and Saurin prove cut elimination for super-exponential systems with fixed points after excluding digging, and explicitly propose studying digging extensions.

This card narrows that research direction to one modal rule family and fixes a forward-thread validity condition. The narrowing and the weaker existential cut-admissibility target are editorial choices.

import_provenance.original_statement: Extend the uniform cut-elimination theorem for μsuperLL∞ to include digging rules, which permit nested exponential modalities, while retaining least and greatest fixed points and the validity condition for non-wellfounded proofs. Bauer and Saurin identify digging as the missing case in their general theorem; suitable explicit restrictions may be necessary.

sentences: The source proposes extending infinitary cut elimination to digging rules.
This card selects one explicit linear modal calculus with least and greatest fixed points.
Digging removes one layer of a repeated diamond modality.
Every infinite proof branch must carry a progressing greatest-fixed-point thread.
The precise target is existence of a valid cut-free proof for each provable sequent.
